notes:
Summary: Tidewater builds real-time conversational assistants and predictive analytics for the maritime industry. They are evaluating Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput and lower unit cost under sustained QPS. Primary ask: dedicated capacity with strict latency SLOs and an auditable SLA appendix for procurement.

Traffic profile and sizing cues: 
- Stated baseline: 40 QPS steady-state (internal analytics averages during business hours).
- Peak spikes: up to 320-360 QPS during port-activity windows and global sync events (30-45 minute bursts).
- Median reply size: ~180 tokens for chat responses; some long reports ~800 tokens for nightly summaries.
- Estimated steady-state token/sec: 40 * 180 = 7,200 tok/s.
- Estimated peak burst token/sec: 360 * 180 = 64,800 tok/s (note: long-summary bursts will push token/sec higher intermittently).

Latency & SLO targets discussed: 
- Business requirement from CTO: p95 interactive chat <= 200 ms (hard), p99 <= 400 ms (aspirational).
- For long-generation jobs (reports): p95 <= 3s acceptable if routed to batch workers.
- Redwood suggestion: single-digit batching for chat path, separate batch pool for long summaries.

Model preferences & routing: 
- Preference for open models: Llama-family 13B quantized for most chat paths; smaller/regressor model for reranking and embeddings.
- Require automatic fallback to a smaller low-latency variant when Dedicated pool is saturated.

Reserved GPU planning & initial recommendation: 
- SE Luca's back-of-envelope: to meet baseline + predictable headroom, start with 8x H100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated pool) with a 2-GPU burst reserve. This supports steady 40 QPS with low p95 for chat and headroom for short bursts.
- Autoscaling policy: allow controlled burst to private burst pool from a separate capacity pool (billing/commit implications to be agreed).
- Sizing note: long-report workloads should be routed to a smaller pool or scheduled off-peak to avoid affecting interactive SLOs.

SLA / procurement conversation notes: 
- Customer needs: 99.9% regional uptime + p95 latency SLOs per model route; audit logs and KMS key access logging required.
- Procurement asks for an SLA appendix that defines SLO measurement windows, penalties, and a mechanism for model variant fallbacks (to avoid downtime).
- Redwood commercial to propose a two-tier SLA: core interactive SLO (p95) and batch SLO (throughput per hour) with clear escalation steps.

POC / Workshop deliverables (explicit): 
1) Measured baseline from Tidewater traffic file (SE to run synthetic replay in Redwood sandbox).
2) Token/sec and GPU throughput mapping (tokens/sec per GPU for candidate models).
3) Recommended reserved GPU commit (initial + burst) and autoscaling policy.
4) Draft SLA appendix with p95/p99 measurement method, regional failover plan, and rollback/fallback rules.
5) Cost model: per-token cost estimates at steady-state and at peak, sensitivity analysis around batching and KV caching.

Quotes / call snippets: 
- CTO Marina Lopez: "We can tolerate a small window of degraded quality for heavy reports, but interactive chat must feel instantaneous—users will not wait >200ms p95."
- Head of Infra: "Need VPC peering and KMS proof before legal will move forward. Also number of GPUs committed affects our budget cycle."

Next actions before workshop: 
- Tidewater to share detailed hourly QPS logs (CSV) and example prompts (by Feb 28).
- Redwood SE to prepare synthetic replay harness and initial token-to-GPU throughput table (Mar 3).
- Commercial to draft preliminary SLA appendix and reserved capacity pricing (Mar 5).

Blockers: Networking sign-off and final budget approval remain the two gating items.
